rows.explainer: 0.29 is our calculated rate ratio, based on combining the SMC Cochrane Review with Tagbor 2016. See "RevMan analysis" here: https://docs.google.com/a/givewell.org/document/d/1mYhJcSBUWOHcIzC7Vzvs_5j26YtPPoBW546hqv7rgaU/edit?usp=sharing. 0.62 is the RR from Tagbor 2016, the weakest effect on malaria incidence that we've obeserved in the 7 RCTs we've seen on SMC.

rows.label: Fraction of annual malaria burden occurring in SMC period (Large effects only (anemia, cognitive, malaria))
rows.explainer: In sites considered suitable for SMC, the median fraction of incidence occurring in the 4 consecutive months of peak transmission was 77% and the mean 75.7% (Supplementary Table S1,2). We therefore assumed that, on average, 75% of the annual burden occurred in the SMC period, but also explored the impact of SMC, if 60% and 90% of annual incidence occurred in the period when SMC was given. Cairns 2012, Pg 9. Note that according to the WHO, 60% is the minimum fraction of incidence occuring in 4 months for an area to be suitable for SMC. WHO SMC Policy Recommendation 2012, Pg 2.

rows.label: Ratio of the reduction in malaria mortality to the reduction in malaria incidence (Large effects only (anemia, cognitive, malaria))
rows.explainer: GW best guess - Our base assumption is that malaria incidence and malaria mortality are related at a 1:1 ratio (e.g. a 71% reduction in malaria incidence leads to a 71% reduction in malaria mortality). In WHO's Africa region, malaria incidence declined by ~40% between 2000 and 2015, and malaria mortality rates declined by ~65% (World Malaria Report 2015, Pg 10, Figure 2.2). Reductions in malaria mortality could be caused by a combination of reductions in malaria incidence and increased access to malaria treatment.

rows.label: Replicability adustment (Large effects only (anemia, cognitive, malaria))
rows.explainer: GW best guess - Our best guess that the significant malaria incidence reduction effects from SMC RCTs would replicate. We have seen evidence for SMC's significant effects on malaria incidence from 7 randomized controlled trials (RCTs included in Meremikwu et al 2012 plus Tagbor 2016.)

rows.label: External validity adjustment (Large effects only (anemia, cognitive, malaria))
rows.explainer: GW best guess - We account for differences in malaria mortality separately, so this external validity adjustment accounts for other differences between the settings of the SMC RCTs in the 2006 "baseline" year and present SMC programs in Sahel regions.
